blocks.text: One image for every environment; config comes from the environment and is validated at startup, so misconfiguration crashes immediately instead of on the first request.

blocks.code:
from pydantic import PostgresDsn, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", secrets_dir="/run/secrets", extra="ignore")
    database_url: PostgresDsn
    openai_api_key: SecretStr | None = None
    embedding_dim: int = 384

blocks.text: A Compose-provided env var beats a stray .env copied into the image, but keep .env out of images anyway.

items: Fail fast: missing DATABASE_URL → ValidationError → exit 1 with a clear message.
`SecretStr` renders as `**********` in logs; call `.get_secret_value()` only at use.
Typed values: "384" becomes an int and invalid values are rejected.

blocks.text: Don't share one .env between local runs and containers: one of the two values is always wrong. Local runs use .env; containers get values from Compose.

Q: "How do you manage config for a containerized FastAPI app?" A: "Twelve-factor: one image, config from env and secret files, loaded and validated by pydantic-settings at startup with SecretStr for sensitive fields, so a missing or invalid value fails fast and the same image runs in every environment."

items: Env beats dotenv; secrets_dir comes after.
Hostnames differ inside vs outside Docker.
